name: Counter 3-5-2 Wing-Back

slots.why: Wide centre-back who defends the channel. Cover is the alternate.
Ball-playing defender starts counters with a forward pass.
Cover centre-back sweeps up behind his partner and the wing-back's space; Defend is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Support wing-back is the safer side and stays back more.
Attacking wing-back is the main wide outlet on the counter.
Supporting holding midfielder screens the back three and passes to the runners.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the counter with runs from deep.
Mezzala breaks forward into the half-space to join the forwards.
Complete Forward or Deep-lying Forward holds up the ball while the others run.
Poacher (or Advanced Forward) finishes the counter and runs in behind.

description: A back-three counter system using wing-backs for width and two forwards as immediate outlets.
whyGood: Three centre-backs protect the box while two forwards keep counter-attacking threat high.
whyThisShape: Three centre-backs with wing-backs for width, a holding midfielder and two forwards ready to break. It defends deep with five or six players and counters through the wing-backs and forwards.
whenToUse: Against stronger opponents who will dominate the ball, or when you have good wing-backs and forwards but a weaker midfield.
whenNotToUse: When you need to dominate the ball, or when your wing-backs are not fit enough to cover the whole flank.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Lower Tempo: Allow the passing structure to form during settled possession; a selected Counter instruction still applies immediately after regains.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Drop Off More Defensive Line: Provide more space in front of the defenders and less behind them, accepting reduced territory.
instructionRationale.Lower Line of Engagement: Let the opposition advance before engaging, keeping space for the forward outlets after a regain.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Release the forward outlets before the opponent recovers.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
